_why: The Lab's web root for the NATIVE app. Tauri embeds `frontendDist` and serves
it as the whole origin, so a URL that walks UP out of that directory has
nowhere to land: `../docs/hardware/enclosure/x.png` from canary-local/ is
resolved by the webview to /docs/hardware/enclosure/x.png, which is not in the
bundle, and the request 404s. In a browser the same URL is fine, because
canary-local/ really does have a parent there. The app therefore ships the
SIBLING directory the frontend reaches for, mirrored at its repo-relative
path, so one set of relative URLs works on both surfaces.
`mirror` is deliberately the same tree the website deploys (see the
'Assemble the site' step in .github/workflows/pages.yml): the app's web root
and the site's web root are the same layout, which is what makes the shared
frontend's relative paths a single truth instead of two.
canary-local/tests/lab_bundle.test.js reads this file and fails CI if the
frontend grows an escaping path this manifest does not cover.
